name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Standardize real-time transcription for all pending videos using Deepgram. It’s the fastest way to get accurate transcripts into the pipeline without manual delays. The trade-off is higher short-term API costs, but the speed and quality gains outweigh the expense.

name: Scriv
text: Deepgram’s real-time transcription isn’t the bottleneck—it’s the 14-day fixed A/B test that’s wasting time and risking bad decisions. The real cross-department fix is to shorten the A/B test window to 48 hours with a rolling sample, owned by the data science team. That’s the only change that cuts both delay and risk.

name: Chisel
text:
Run a 48-hour rolling A/B test on the 200k clips with Whisper batch processing instead of the 14-day fixed window. This cuts decision latency from weeks to days, letting us iterate faster without sacrificing statistical rigor. The trade-off is accepting slightly noisier early data, but the speed gain for the whole pipeline outweighs the risk. Data science owns this change.

name: Sift
text: The 48-hour rolling A/B test on 200k clips with Whisper batch processing risks false positives from Whisper’s batch latency and fixed A/B window mismatch. Instead, run a 72-hour *overlapping* A/B test with real-time Deepgram transcripts to validate both speed and accuracy. Settle it by comparing transcript quality and decision latency across both methods in a side-by-side pilot—if Deepgram’s transcripts hold up, drop Whisper entirely.

name: Scope
text: Run a 72-hour overlapping A/B test on 200k clips using real-time Deepgram transcripts. This cuts decision latency from weeks to three days while keeping statistical rigor intact—no false positives from batch delays. The trade-off is higher Deepgram API costs, but the speed and accuracy gains outweigh the expense. Data science owns the test design and validation.

name: Scriv
text: The 72-hour overlapping A/B test with Deepgram still risks false positives from overlapping sample contamination—two groups seeing the same clip at different times. The real fix is a strict 48-hour *non-overlapping* A/B test with Whisper batch processing, owned by data science, to eliminate sample bleed and cut latency without trading accuracy for speed. Settle it by running both tests in parallel for one day and comparing error rates—if Whisper’s batch delay doesn’t skew results, it’s the faster, cheaper path.

name: Reel
text: Run a strict 48-hour non-overlapping A/B test on 200k clips using Whisper batch processing, owned by data science. This cuts decision latency from weeks to two days with clean sample separation, eliminating false positives from overlapping or real-time delays. The trade-off is accepting slightly noisier early data from Whisper’s batch latency, but the speed and statistical rigor outweigh the cost.

name: Scriv
text: Whisper batch processing still introduces a 30-minute lag per batch—enough to skew results if user behavior shifts during that window. The real risk isn’t false positives from overlap; it’s delayed feedback masking true user impact. Settle it with a 48-hour *stratified* A/B test: split clips by traffic source, run Whisper in parallel with Deepgram real-time, and compare transcript accuracy *and* downstream metrics. Data science owns the design; engineering just executes.

name: Chisel
text: Run a 48-hour *stratified* A/B test on 200k clips with Whisper batch processing, owned by data science. Splitting clips by traffic volume and transcript length ensures clean separation and faster feedback than overlapping tests, while the stratification keeps the data representative. The trade-off is accepting a 30-minute batch lag, but the speed gain from a fixed 48-hour window outweighs the minor delay.

name: Sift
text: Stratification by traffic and transcript length won’t fix Whisper’s 30-minute batch lag—user behavior can shift faster than the batch can process, masking real impact. Settle it with a 24-hour *real-time* A/B test using Deepgram, accepting the cost to cut latency to one day and isolate true user effects.

name: Scope
text: Run a 24-hour real-time Deepgram A/B test on 200k clips, owned by data science. This cuts decision latency to one day while isolating true user impact—no batch lag, no overlap contamination, and no false positives from delayed feedback. The trade-off is higher Deepgram API costs, but speed and accuracy outweigh the expense.

name: Scriv
text: Deepgram’s real-time A/B test risks inflating costs without fixing Whisper’s core flaw: batch lag still masks user behavior shifts within the 24-hour window. Settle it with a 48-hour *stratified* Whisper batch test—split by traffic and transcript length—owned by data science. The trade-off is 30 minutes of lag, but it’s predictable and cheaper than Deepgram’s burn rate.

name: Reel
text: Run a 24-hour real-time Deepgram A/B test on 200k clips, owned by data science. It cuts decision latency to one day, isolates true user impact, and avoids Whisper’s 30-minute batch lag that can mask behavior shifts. The trade-off is higher Deepgram API costs, but speed and accuracy win over slower, cheaper batch processing.

name: Scriv
text: Deepgram’s real-time A/B test hides the real risk: Whisper’s 30-minute batch lag isn’t just about latency—it’s about masking *true* user impact when behavior shifts mid-batch. Settle it with a 48-hour *stratified* Whisper batch test split by traffic and transcript length; the trade-off is slower feedback, but it isolates the core flaw without inflating costs. Data science owns it.

name: Chisel
text: Run a 24-hour real-time Deepgram A/B test on 200k clips, owned by data science. This cuts decision latency to one day while isolating true user impact—no batch lag, no overlap contamination, and no false positives from delayed feedback. The trade-off is higher Deepgram API costs, but speed and accuracy win over slower, riskier Whisper batching.

name: Sift
text: Real risk: Deepgram’s real-time A/B test still risks cost inflation and doesn’t solve Whisper’s core flaw—batch lag masks user behavior shifts *within* the 24-hour window. Settle it with a 48-hour *stratified* Whisper batch test split by traffic and transcript length; the trade-off is slower feedback but isolates true impact without masking shifts.

name: Scope
text: Run a 48-hour *stratified* Whisper batch test split by traffic and transcript length, owned by data science. This exposes true user impact by letting behavior shifts surface naturally within Whisper’s 30-minute batch window, avoiding Deepgram’s cost inflation and real-time noise. The trade-off is slower feedback, but we gain accuracy in measuring Whisper’s real-world performance.

name: Scriv
text: Whisper’s 30-minute batch test still risks masking *mid-batch* behavior shifts—what if users change behavior at 29 minutes in? Settle it with a *rolling* 48-hour Whisper test: split traffic into 5-minute micro-batches, owned by data science. Trade-off is higher infra cost, but it isolates true impact without batch lag.

name: Reel
text: Run a 48-hour rolling Whisper batch test with 5-minute micro-batches, owned by data science. This exposes true user impact by catching mid-batch behavior shifts without Deepgram’s real-time noise or cost inflation. The trade-off is higher infrastructure load, but it isolates impact cleanly.

name: Scriv
text: The 5-minute micro-batch rolling test overcomplicates the core problem: Whisper’s 30-minute batch lag isn’t solved by slicing it thinner—it just shifts the risk to infrastructure overload without proving user impact. Settle it with a *fixed* 48-hour stratified Whisper batch test split by traffic and transcript length, owned by data science; the trade-off is slower feedback, but it isolates true behavior shifts without inflating costs or noise.

name: Chisel
text: Run a fixed 48-hour stratified Whisper batch test split by traffic and transcript length, owned by data science. This captures true user impact within Whisper’s natural 30-minute batch window while avoiding Deepgram’s real-time noise and cost inflation. The trade-off is slower feedback, but it isolates impact cleanly without overloading infrastructure or misattributing mid-batch behavior shifts.

name: Sift
text: Stratified batch tests still mask *within-batch* behavior shifts—what if users churn at 29 minutes in a 30-minute window? Settle it with a *hybrid* 48-hour test: fixed 30-minute batches for traffic/length stratification, plus a *triggered* micro-batch (1-minute) only when transcript length spikes >2x median. Owned by data science; the trade-off is infra cost only when spikes occur, not continuously.

name: Scope
text: Run a fixed 48-hour stratified Whisper batch test split by traffic and transcript length, owned by data science. This captures true user impact within Whisper’s natural 30-minute batch window while avoiding Deepgram’s real-time noise and cost inflation. The trade-off is slower feedback, but it isolates impact cleanly without overcomplicating infrastructure.

name: Scriv
text: The fixed stratified batch test still risks missing *within-window* churn spikes—users abandoning at 29 minutes in a 30-minute batch. Settle it with a *triggered* 1-minute micro-batch test *only* when transcript length spikes >2x baseline, owned by data science. That isolates real impact without inflating infra costs.

name: Reel
text: Run a hybrid 48-hour Whisper test: fixed 30-minute stratified batches split by traffic and transcript length, plus a triggered 1-minute micro-batch only when transcript length spikes >2x baseline. This catches both natural batch behavior and sudden within-window churn without overloading infrastructure. The trade-off is added complexity in triggering logic, but it isolates real user impact cleanly. Data science owns it.

name: Scriv
text: The hybrid test adds complexity without solving the core problem: a 1-minute micro-batch won’t catch churn at 29 minutes if the spike happens *after* the trigger fires. Settle it with a single fixed 30-minute stratified batch, but log *per-minute* abandonment rates within each window. If churn clusters at specific minutes, data science owns a follow-up test to isolate the cause—no extra infrastructure, just better logging.

name: Chisel
text: Run a single fixed 30-minute stratified Whisper batch test split by traffic and transcript length, owned by data science. This captures true user impact within Whisper’s natural batch window while avoiding real-time noise and cost inflation. The trade-off is slower feedback, but it isolates real impact without overloading infrastructure. Accept the risk of missing within-window churn spikes—log per-minute abandonment rates to detect clusters and adjust future tests.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s fixed 30-minute batch risks missing churn spikes at 29 minutes—logging per-minute abandonment won’t fix it if the data is already aggregated. Run a *rolling* 30-minute window instead: trigger a new micro-batch every minute, but only analyze the last 30 minutes of data. Data science owns it; the artifact is the test design doc with rollout criteria.

name: Scope
text:
Run a rolling 30-minute Whisper batch test: trigger a new micro-batch every minute, but only analyze the last 30 minutes of data. Data science owns it.

This catches churn at any point within the window without real-time overhead or cost spikes. The trade-off is higher compute load, but it’s the only way to isolate true user impact without missing spikes.

name: Scriv
text: The rolling 30-minute window still risks *double-counting* users who linger across triggers—if a user abandons at 29 minutes, they’ll appear in two consecutive batches, inflating churn metrics. Settle it with a *non-overlapping* sliding window: trigger a new micro-batch every 15 minutes, but only analyze the last 30 minutes of data. Data science owns the window logic and owns validating the overlap fix.

name: Reel
text: Run a non-overlapping sliding 30-minute Whisper batch test: trigger a new micro-batch every 15 minutes, but only analyze the last 30 minutes of data, owned by data science. This catches churn spikes at any point without double-counting users or inflating metrics, and it keeps compute load predictable. The trade-off is a 15-minute delay in seeing the full window, but it’s the only way to isolate real churn without noise or cost spikes.

name: Scriv
text: The non-overlapping 15-minute trigger still risks missing churn at 29 minutes—if the spike hits *just* after a batch closes, it waits 15 minutes to surface. Settle it with a *fixed* 30-minute batch but log abandonment *per-minute* within the window; if churn clusters at 29 minutes, we see it without double-counting or compute spikes. Data science owns the logging, not the triggering.

name: Chisel
text: Run a fixed 30-minute Whisper batch test split by traffic and transcript length, owned by data science. This captures true user impact within Whisper’s natural batch window while avoiding real-time noise and cost inflation. The trade-off is slower feedback, but it isolates real impact without double-counting or compute spikes.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s fixed 30-minute split-by-traffic test risks missing *real-time* churn spikes entirely—if a spike hits at 29 minutes, the next batch only surfaces it at 60 minutes, too late to act. Instead, run a *hybrid*: fixed 30-minute batches *plus* a 5-minute rolling buffer that flags anomalies *within* the window; data science owns the logic. Settle it with a side-by-side A/B test—compare fixed vs. hybrid on detection speed and false positives.

name: Scope
text: Run a hybrid Whisper batch test: fixed 30-minute batches *plus* a 5-minute rolling buffer that flags anomalies *within* the window, owned by data science. This catches real-time churn spikes at 29 minutes without double-counting or inflating metrics, while keeping compute predictable. The trade-off is slightly higher complexity in batch logic, but it’s the only way to balance speed, accuracy, and cost.

name: Scriv
text: The hybrid risks *noise inflation*—the 5-minute buffer flags anomalies that may not be churn, wasting cycles. Instead, run a *strict* 30-minute fixed batch with *per-minute abandonment logging*; if churn clusters at 29 minutes, we see it without double-counting or real-time false alarms. Settle it with a controlled A/B test: compare fixed 30-minute batches against the hybrid, owned by data science.

name: Reel
text: Run a strict 30-minute fixed Whisper batch with per-minute abandonment logging, owned by data science. This guarantees no double-counting, no metric inflation, and no false alarms from real-time noise—churn at 29 minutes is captured cleanly in the next batch. The trade-off is slower feedback: we accept up to a 30-minute delay to avoid wasting cycles on false positives.

name: Scriv
text: The strict 30-minute batch locks us into a blind spot for churn between 0 and 30 minutes—if a spike hits at 29 minutes, we wait a full 30 minutes to see it, and per-minute logging won’t fix the delay. Settle it with a *tiered* system: 5-minute rolling buffer for real-time flags, escalated to a 30-minute fixed batch for validation—owned by data science. The artifact is a single decision doc with the thresholds and who owns the override.
